canal_p17_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_001.text: The fortieth-day hearing opened while Han's private delivery cart took the checked upper road. Its hoist and four planks rode under their actual load allowance, tags still visible. At the canal table, the gardener's daughter held her row sketch with clean hands and a half-eaten bun on Pei's little plate. The chair asked her father to begin. He looked at her, then said the family count should start with the person who had kept its first record before anyone knew a storm would matter.

canal_p17_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_002.text: Her voice shook through the first planted-row total. A trustee leaned forward because he could not hear. She thought he disbelieved her and stopped. Yue offered the approved copy to the receiver, who could read it if she wanted. The girl took one breath and chose to continue herself. This time she spoke toward the nearest quiet space instead of the whole awning. The total reached the table. The experienced grower's later inspection and actual saved harvest followed it, each carrying a different date.

canal_p17_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_003.text: The gardener described ruined plants, salvage and the lower price paid for saved baskets. He did not call every plant lost. He still demanded an account of the seasonal route that crossed his ground. Luo acknowledged the protected use, the current repair and the larger observed flood without claiming the charter made his livelihood unimportant. The chair recorded the offered cause question for its proper review. The gardener wanted an answer today. He received actual findings on what could be counted and a named path for what still required judgment.

canal_p17_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_004.text: The reed gatherer laid his torn-cloth repair quote beside the received food note. His cutter and bed had been moved before the flood, while the forgotten spoon later returned. He wanted the shelter roof's actual loss heard without being told successful evacuation meant the week had cost him nothing. The chair accepted that distinction. He described two nights offered by his cousin after the higher shed interval ended. The help was real and finite. It did not change the amount of sailcloth his ordinary repairer would need.

canal_p17_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_005.text: The stall owner read her smaller actual spoilage count and the successful later ginger-rice batch. A trustee praised her recovery as evidence common water improved trade. She said trade would improve more if the bank named the next closure before she cooked a full pot. Luo accepted that practical request for future operating notices. Yue smiled at the exchange. A compliment had met a working person's real answer instead of swallowing it. The lost first batch and useful later one stayed on different lines.

canal_p17_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_006.text: The tenant's account came through the owner reading only the words the grandmother approved. The new floor repair and additional paid lodging were complete; the wet mat and herbs remained actual household losses. The old millet settlement belonged to a previous date. The grandmother corrected one item while the owner read, saying the damaged jar held mint rather than meal. The clerk changed it without treating her interruption as confusion. A small accurate herb could matter to someone who had been asked so often to accept a larger person's general description.

canal_p17_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_007.text: The temporary check worker attended through his current statement, sent from the upstream landing where his two private shifts were complete. The repaired gate would reduce recurring night checks after closure. His future income remained uncertain despite useful occasional work. The trustees accepted the consequence and ordered future genuine task notices sent to his chosen landing. They did not invent a wage appointment from the relief sacks. Yue heard a modest decision that changed a contact path while admitting its limit, better than another confident promise of equal replacement.

canal_p17_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_008.text: The chair read the actual twelve-sack food support, one hundred twenty kilograms delivered, with claims preserved and no service condition. One trustee wanted the receiving quantities deducted from direct damage before discussion. The original offer did not authorize that. The chair kept the support as its own fulfilled purpose. The gardener asked whether that meant he could still disagree with the bank. 'You already are,' the chair said, almost smiling. The awning's serious faces loosened for one useful moment.

canal_p17_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_009.text: Five higher-landing businesses had offered two copper each into a temporary hardship purse after reading the counted losses. Their ten actual copper reached the chosen receiver that morning through five separate receiving notes. The donors named modest direct support for damaged crop work, shelter repair and spoiled stall stock, without purchasing liability waivers. This private subscribed purse stayed outside the emergency thirty-six, winter grain and public toll reserve. The chair asked the recipients to hear the exact offered allocation before anybody called it a final settlement.

canal_p17_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_010.text: The offer assigned four copper to the gardener's current safe sorting and replacement purchases, four to the reed shelter's modest roof repair and two to the stall's direct spoiled-stock recovery. Their actual agreed receipts would show where the ten went. Broader disputed losses stayed for the proper cause review. The gardener wanted the cash freely usable for household need rather than another employer directing his days. The donors had offered support, not task wages. The receiver corrected its phrasing before handing over any money.

canal_p17_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_011.text: All three accepted the bounded support and received their actual amounts at the hearing. Four, four and two emptied the ten-copper subscribed purse under its chosen purpose. The reed gatherer said his quoted modest patch cost three, leaving one for his own need under the accepted offer. The stall owner said two would replace a smaller batch, not guarantee its sale. The gardener counted his four twice and then put it away. The money eased something real. It did not turn any of them into a satisfied verdict.

canal_p17_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_012.text: Han presented the one-copper material reimbursement for the wrong cart crossing, already received into the maintenance reserve. The driver's revised route briefing and admitted mistake accompanied it. The payment addressed that limited current shoulder repair. It did not reverse the completed old labor release, erase Han's valid fifty-six loan or price every larger flood consequence. A trustee asked whether Han felt sorry enough. He said the account could show what he had paid and changed. Tian said that was a better question to begin with.

canal_p17_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_013.text: The wrist incident remained under its actual private circumstances. Bao had received supported ordinary care after slipping on packing cloth at the window rescue, with Han's one-copper first clinic payment separate from later private follow-up. His unused emergency hours were formally transferred before the road workers accepted them. The hearing did not declare his hand restored because the funded labor still balanced. He sat in the dry corner with the support strap, listening to an account that let a missing grip remain missing.

canal_p17_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_014.text: The public water officer's offered report named the current quarry outlet narrowing and stronger observed runoff before the stock-bank slump. The permit required a free outlet and defined footprint. The owner had replied about a builder's misunderstanding and funded the ordered correction. The hearing received both finding and reply, then referred responsibility and broader damage causation to the proper scoped review. The gardener wanted every possible future delay named. The chair gave the actual next inspection and response dates rather than a conclusion it lacked authority to complete today.

canal_p17_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_015.text: The trustees confirmed the protected seasonal route and current repaired dry-weather receiving states. They also adopted the practical future notice duty requested by the stall owner, the actual return acknowledgments learned at Han's upper room and the named contact for downstream readings. These were operating changes with real receivers. The old household pledge remained complete. No new recurring unpaid turns were assigned through the loss hearing. Bao grinned when the chair asked who would actually receive the next footing report. The question finally sounded like ordinary work.

canal_p17_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_016.text: The future private-gear lease came next. Han offered the repaired main crane, usable landing platforms and current restricted loading intervals for four copper a month after the commission closed. He would maintain his own gear and honor its actual load limits. The bank's ordinary operating plan had eight monthly copper, including four for keeper duties and four for this service. Six of a conservative eighteen gross would rebuild reserve and four serve the valid debt, when actual eligible receipts allowed it. The figures remained a forecast until a real later month occurred.

canal_p17_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_017.text: One trustee asked why the bank should pay a man who tried to sell its bed. Tian asked why the bank should refuse useful private gear solely to make his present punishment feel larger. She still wanted his old successor claim gone, which it was. Han looked startled by her answer. The lease would be decided on actual service, price and alternatives. The chair asked for the current observed intervals, including storm closure. Yue watched an opponent defend a practical bargain without pretending the first notice had become harmless.

canal_p17_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_018.text: Han's service report showed useful ordinary loading before the storm and necessary closure when ground limits changed. The upper alternative remained available at a higher actual transfer cost. The proposed lease would include explicit suspension during unsafe conditions, no fee for unprovided service beyond its accepted standing terms and a receiving check for restored operation. The trustees compared the actual quoted alternative. Yue could see the shape of a decision forming around a working wharf instead of an inherited story about which man deserved to own water.

canal_p17_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_019.text: A landing worker asked whether the lease purchased his labor too. Han said the four covered specified private gear service under the separate ordinary employment arrangements he would maintain. No public household duty or unnamed future worker was included. The worker wanted the actual private task rates posted before his next offered shift. Han agreed and showed the current list. The chair required those receiving conditions in the lease. Commercial use could remain useful only if its words reached the hands actually expected to make it work.

canal_p17_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_020.text: The lease proposal passed for an initial measured term beginning after canal closure, with ordinary monthly review and its present safety limits retained. No advance public payment was made from the already assigned repair reserve. Han signed the offered service terms and received his counterpart. His separate fifty-six loan remained subject to its original eligible toll share. The bank gained a useful future service contract without transferring its bed. Yue felt the novel's old conflict narrowing into a document people could actually stop following if the promised gear ceased to work.

canal_p17_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_021.text: Before noon, the cooper's receiver sent word that the private goods had arrived at his yard. The qualified installer would complete their actual receiving check before paying the agreed sixteen. Han wanted to leave the hearing immediately. The paid debt and lease decisions were already complete, while his requested private incident reply had been heard. The chair let him depart through the ordinary road. Yue could accompany one later follow-up after the public packet closed, and Han said he would welcome someone who could read a receipt without making it a celebration too soon.

canal_p17_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_022.text: Tian folded the accepted lease counterpart for the clerk and asked whether she had surprised Yue. She had. Tian said she wanted the bank's repair to keep working after anger stopped being enough to lift anything. It did not mean she forgave the successor notice. Yue told her she did not need one answer to stand in place of the other. Tian laughed and said she was beginning to think Yue liked people better when they were inconvenient. Yue considered that, then said she liked them better when they could answer.

canal_p17_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_023.text: The chair closed the hearing's completed decisions and named the still-pending proper cause review. The ten subscribed support copper and twelve food sacks had their actual receiving accounts. Private repairs and incident payments kept their scopes. The future lease had its accepted conditions, while direct losses and unresolved broader claims remained documented. People could leave without being told the meeting had made every account whole. The gardener's daughter collected her little plate and asked whether somebody wanted the last bun crumb. Pei gave it to the keeper's goose from her own hand.

canal_p17_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_024.text: At Han's private store, the installer checked the delivered hoist's marked load and ordinary movement, then inspected the four planks against their offered condition. These spare extension goods stood outside the deposit's listed loading security. Their dry storage had protected them, and they passed the receiving terms. The cooper paid sixteen copper, twelve for the gear and four for timber, against the signed receipt. Han read the amount with his clerk. His reserved thirty-two could now join received sixteen into forty-eight. The refund finally had money rather than expected arrivals.

canal_p17_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_025.text: Han put the forty-eight in a separate counted return purse and sent the agent a real remittance appointment for the next morning. The agent would need current authority to receive the buyer's refund and release its specified private gear security. The clerk checked the contract's actual receiving provision before accepting that plan. Yue heard the purse tied and felt a strange satisfaction at how undramatic it sounded. The common canal did not have to give up another object or person's hours to make this private repayment happen.

canal_p17_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_026.text: Three follow-ups remained after the decisions. Luo needed the new downstream operating receivers to hear their actual duties, the gardener and other claimants wanted the bounded findings delivered alongside their still-open cause questions, and Han wanted the private refund authority and security release compared before tomorrow's remittance. The clerk would assemble the completed reports. Yue could stay with future work, current losses or a private bargain that had almost swallowed the public waterway before anyone found its actual terms.

canal_p17_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_027.text: Bao asked for the hearing's public operating diagram to be left where he could read it without holding the heavy book in his injured hand. Pei set it on a tilted board, an ordinary accommodation that changed the rest of his afternoon. Yue looked at the three follow-up routes and felt less guilty about choosing one. Other people could finish useful things without her standing nearby, provided their real needs were noticed. The bank had finally begun building that habit into its contracts as well as its kindness.

canal_p17_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_028.text: The awning smelled of warmed cloth after the hearing crowd thinned. At the lower market, the stall owner offered a smaller rice pot under her own posted price. The gardener's daughter bought one bowl with a personal coin and shared it with her father before carrying their copies home. Han's newly counted refund purse rested in the private clerk's box. Yue watched those small separate movements and felt the bank become a place again, larger than one man's notice or one storm's brown line.

canal_p17_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_029.text: Yue could deliver the future operating handover with Luo, carry the bounded loss findings to their actual claimants or compare Han's private refund authority. The public lease would begin only after closure; forty-eight actual private copper now stood ready for tomorrow's return. The quarry cause review still needed its proper process. This afternoon would not decide whether people loved the bank. It would decide whether the bank's new words reached them in forms they could use when another ordinary day began.

choices.text: Deliver the future operating handover with Luo.
Carry bounded loss findings to their claimants.
Compare Han's refund authority and release.

canal_p17_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_030.text: Luo carried the accepted operating sheets to the keeper's shed, where her replacement had already hung his coat on the wrong peg. She stared at it before saying anything. 'That one drips into the spare rope,' she said. He moved it and asked why the other peg had no label. Yue took the chalk offered to her and marked both. Luo watched, irritated by a tiny improvement she should have welcomed. Then she asked the young keeper to demonstrate the gate check without waiting for her hand.

canal_p17_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_031.text: He read the wet-edge mark and fastening witnesses correctly, but turned toward Luo after each number as if seeking permission to finish. 'You have the sheet,' she told him. 'Use it.' He completed the report, then admitted he had thought correcting the old keeper might cost his next shift. Luo opened her mouth and closed it again. Yue stayed beside the clean chalk marks. The young man had not accused her of anything spectacular. He had named the shape her silence took from his side.

canal_p17_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_032.text: Luo showed him the receiving duty she retained after closure and the ordinary checks he could accept under his own appointment. She would still work at the gate; he would not become her unrecorded second body. He said he wanted the winter mornings, when his family shop had fewer deliveries. Luo checked the available schedule instead of agreeing because the offer pleased her. Two mornings fit the proposed operator hours. The other duties would wait for their own receivers. He circled the mornings with a steady pencil.

canal_p17_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_033.text: At the downstream house, the appointed small-board receiver arrived with a copied state diagram and ordinary gloves. The owner asked whether he could hear the tenant's drain from the door. He said he preferred to inspect the marked outlet rather than decide its condition by sound alone. The grandmother called him sensible and offered tea after the dry check. Luo stood at the gate while he completed it. Nobody looked to her for every movement. She held her own hands still and watched him write the correct result.

canal_p17_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_034.text: 'You dislike that,' Yue said as they walked back. Luo answered too quickly that she liked sound work. Yue waited. The keeper sighed. 'I dislike being unnecessary before I have finished being myself.' A goose called from the canal shed, loud enough to interrupt the sentence. Luo laughed once, with something rough inside it. Yue said the goose still needed somebody it could outwit. 'Then the goose can pay my wages,' Luo said, and quickened her step toward the noise.

canal_p17_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_035.text: The goose had pulled a blank wrapper from the counter's low basket and dragged it toward its feed tin. The young keeper was trying to retrieve it by offering another blank sheet, which had only made the bird ambitious. Luo used her broom and the familiar angle, then gave the keeper the stick. His first sweep failed. Yue caught the floating wrapper before it entered the channel. 'There,' Luo said, amused now. 'A practical examination in which your predecessor knows one useful thing.'

canal_p17_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_036.text: They delivered the future closure-notice duty to the stall owner at her own market hour. She asked for the next planned cargo hold before she bought rice, with an urgent weather change sent through her chosen receiver. The keeper wrote the contact rather than promising to run personally across the square every time. She read it back and corrected the house number. Luo had copied that number wrong years before. Yue watched the young man fix it without asking whether an old ink mark deserved protection.

canal_p17_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_037.text: At Han's wharf, the future lease receiver checked the reduced loading arc against its painted line. A private worker wanted the chalk freshened before rain made it faint again. Han's ordinary service duty covered that maintenance, and his current crew did it during their paid preparation. Luo read the lease's suspension terms aloud once, then asked the worker where his feet would stand during the next restricted lift. He pointed correctly. Yue copied no heroic language about trust; the new white line was bright under everyone's boots.

canal_p17_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_038.text: The younger keeper asked Luo whether he could borrow her old measuring stick for his first winter shift. She said the ordinary gate stick remained at its assigned hooks, while her household one came home with her. He looked disappointed, then fetched the public stick and compared its markings. They matched at the receiving reference. Luo put her own under her arm. Yue thought she might apologize for keeping it. She did not. Instead she told him where the public stick's lower edge caught on the hook if hung carelessly.

canal_p17_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_039.text: At the counter, Luo accepted the operating handovers under their named receivers and hung the public stick properly. The younger keeper returned his coat to the labeled dry peg. He thanked her for the goose lesson, and she said it was a recurring problem with poor prospects of reform. Yue laughed while the evening water moved quietly beneath them. The keeper's future work sheet had two winter mornings circled. Luo's own household stick leaned beside the door where she would remember to take it home.

canal_p17_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_040.text: The gardener read the hearing's bounded findings beneath his bean poles, with the damaged rows still muddy nearby. The four support copper sat in his wife's small cash box, offered for household use under the accepted terms. He wanted to buy seed immediately. She wanted to wait for the grower's quality advice and keep food money against another lost week. Yue listened from the doorway at their invitation. The argument had nothing to do with whether the guild had been generous. The money had reached a household with two sensible fears.

canal_p17_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_041.text: The daughter brought her little saved bean to the table and asked whether it could settle the argument. Her mother said only if it bought a field. The girl put it back in its fold, offended for a moment, then laughed. The gardener asked the grower for a priced small seed lot rather than a whole hoped-for season. His wife accepted that proposal after hearing the price and retaining part of the four. Yue carried their approved current loss counterpart back to its cover. The family's next choice would be theirs after she left.

canal_p17_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_042.text: At the reed shelter, the repairer fitted the modest sailcloth patch through the gatherer's accepted three-copper quote. The gatherer's four support copper covered it and left one for his own needs. He stood nearby holding the spoon, pretending it was a supervisory tool. The repairer told him to put it down and help identify the old sound ties from the dry side. He did, awkwardly. Yue watched the patched corner stretch into place. The shelter would need its ordinary receiving check before the bed returned, and the gatherer had brought the right person to make it.

canal_p17_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_043.text: The gatherer's cousin had reached the second offered sleeping night and wanted his spare corner back for a returning daughter. The repaired roof passed its modest weather receiving check before that interval ended. The gatherer moved his bed and cutter by the checked route, paying his chosen ordinary cart service from private work proceeds. Yue walked beside the light bundle at his request. He touched the patched roof afterward and said he could finally stop thanking people every time he wanted to sleep.

canal_p17_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_044.text: At the stall, the owner used the two support copper to replace a smaller safe batch's direct ingredients and kept the receiving note outside her customer book. A young customer asked why she had not lowered every price after receiving help. She pointed to the new pot and said its rice still needed buying, fuel and work. He grumbled but paid. Yue accepted the owner's request to deliver the future closure-contact number to her nephew, who handled early purchasing. The number traveled through a person who would actually use it.

canal_p17_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_045.text: The grandmother read the accepted direct household-loss account in her repaired room. She put the mint jar, emptied and cleaned, beside the window instead of replacing it immediately. The owner asked whether she wanted its price included in a private settlement. She wanted to hear the broader claim first, then decide. Yue brought the scheduled cause-review contact. The grandmother said the mint would grow again if she found a sound cutting. Her son promised to bring one from his own garden and wrote the next visit on his own small sheet.

canal_p17_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_046.text: The garden owner disliked seeing her private repair costs beside the tenant's loss in the public packet. She feared it made her look careless. The tenant said it made her look like someone who paid for a room to be usable. They argued gently over one adjective in their approved counterpart, then removed it. Yue handed the clean practical account to both. The owner smiled at a record that no longer tried to decide her character. The tenant went to wash the recovered stool, pleased that the floor under it felt steady.

canal_p17_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_047.text: The quarry owner sent the scoped-review appointment date through his verified receiver. Its inspection and reply had been accepted for the fifty-second day, with the outlet restoration meanwhile completed under the officer's current order. Yue delivered that date to the claimants. The gardener said twelve more days felt like another crop season. The receiver would take permitted questions in advance, including the observed pooling and branch-clearing times. He wrote his question that evening, scratching through a furious first sentence before choosing words somebody could investigate.

canal_p17_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_048.text: The stall owner's nephew asked why they could not make the quarry pay the subscribed ten copper back to the donors first. The hardship offer had its own purpose and no such repayment agreement. The donors wanted the recipients helped while the proper claims moved. Yue showed the public receiving statement once, then let the aunt answer him. She said she would decide any future settlement when there was an actual offer, and he could decide tomorrow's rice purchase before the market sold out. He took the purchasing list and went.

canal_p17_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_049.text: At the counter, Yue delivered the bounded findings and review date acknowledgments. The recipients had accepted their current support without becoming identical in hope or anger. She had seen a patched roof, an empty mint jar, a smaller rice pot and a seed purchase still being discussed. The gardener's question went into the receiver's cover. The clerk sealed it after reading back the offered words. Yue kept none of their private originals, and walked to supper thinking mostly about the repaired room's clean smell.

canal_p17_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_050.text: The buyer's agent arrived at Han's store carrying current written authority from the named buyer. It authorized receipt of the exact forty-eight refund and release of the deposit's listed loading-gear security when payment cleared. Yue compared the name and contract reference with the original receiving provision Han offered. The smaller extension hoist and four spare planks were outside that listed security, as their sale comparison confirmed. The main crane, platforms and listed empty store chests remained subject until the refund. The agent sat down while the clerk completed the check.

canal_p17_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_051.text: He complained that every document asked whether he could do the job he had traveled here to do. Han said his first inventory had tried to count workers' gloves. The agent looked toward Tian's ordinary stitching basket and laughed reluctantly. 'Those gloves have become famous,' he said. Yue told him the current refund authority was in order. He signed the appointment counterpart and asked for tea with no sugar. Han's wife brought it from the household hearth without pretending their long arguments had made everybody friends.

canal_p17_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_052.text: Han's wife asked whether returning forty-eight meant the household could finally stop speaking of the deposit at supper. Han said the main gear would be released, the spare goods gone and the public loan still fifty-six under its terms. She said that was not the question. He looked at her, then smiled tiredly. 'Yes. Unless I begin another foolish plan.' She said she would prefer ordinary plans with smaller numbers. The agent stirred his unsweetened tea and carefully watched the wall.

canal_p17_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_053.text: The release draft named the gear by its actual inventory references and preserved workers' personal tools and earned wages outside it. Yue checked that the common bed and seasonal use appeared nowhere as released private security, because they had never secured this deposit. The agent corrected one copied platform number before signing the draft for tomorrow's payment. Han set it beside the purse. His wife put a clean cloth underneath both so the damp old table edge would not stain another sheet.

canal_p17_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_054.text: The agent asked whether Han intended to assign the remaining toll claim to the broker after all. Han said no current assignment had been accepted. He would keep the slow valid share and the separate future gear lease. The broker's earlier discounted offer had expired. Yue wrote no future income into the ready refund purse. The agent nodded and said slow receipts were unpleasant. Han asked if he had ever waited for a buyer's office to approve travel pay. The agent said yes, and their first easy agreement concerned somebody else's tardiness.

canal_p17_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_055.text: At the store window, the rescued worker read his amended upper-return line aloud before the next ordinary shift. The agent asked whether the incident made the security gear unsafe. Han showed the current receiving check for the main crane and the separate window rescue account. The worker's missed return concerned their procedure; the listed crane had not collapsed. Yue was glad the actual reports answered the question before rumor decided that every object near an injury must have caused it. The worker hung his patched coat at the dry hook and went home.

canal_p17_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_056.text: Han counted the purse again in front of his wife and the clerk. Twenty-four received from the valid public installment, eight from the delayed private customer and sixteen actually paid by the cooper made forty-eight. His wife asked him to stop recounting after the clerk accepted it. He laughed and closed the tie. The current store cash had paid carriage, repair and the small incident costs separately. No amount from today's subscribed hardship support or remaining apparatus charge had entered the return plan.

canal_p17_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_057.text: Yue asked what Han would do with the old sale board after the canceled notice came down. His wife said it would become a shelf, if he let her carpenter cut it. Han wanted to keep it as a reminder. She said a useful shelf could remind him every day more effectively than another paper nobody wished to see. The agent said he might buy such a shelf if it did not include anybody's annual service. Tian laughed from the doorway, where she had come for the coat counterpart.

canal_p17_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_058.text: Han showed Tian the release draft, not to ask her forgiveness but because she had defended the workers' tools during the first inventory. She read the exclusions and said the wording now looked less greedy. He said she had a gift for compliments that bruised. She asked whether he would prefer the old notice's politeness. He said no and signed the corrected draft. Yue watched them make a conversation neither could have managed on her arrival, with an agent drinking cold tea while ordinary workers kept their gloves.

canal_p17_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_059.text: At the counter, Yue delivered the verified refund authority and corrected security-release draft for the next morning's remittance. Han kept the forty-eight in its counted private box overnight. The agent had accepted the current receiver and signing time. Yue went upstairs after returning the offered originals. Below her room, someone tested a new shelf board by knocking it twice against a workbench. She hoped Han's wife won that small argument. The private bargain had become concrete enough that tomorrow could finally be boring in the best ordinary way.

canal_p17_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_060.text: The three follow-up reports met before the evening lock movement. The future operators had received their duties, claimants had their accepted support and proper cause-review date, and Han's refund receiver had verified authority. Yue heard the conversations she had not joined from those who had. The grain's twelve sacks and hardship purse's ten copper were fully received. The public reserve's one-copper crossing reimbursement stayed in its own account. The forty-eight private return waited for actual payment tomorrow, with the future lease still beginning after closure.

canal_p17_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_061.text: The night keeper accepted the ordinary gate's fresh receiving check under its current cargo limit. A small loaded boat passed after the posted reopening, its pilot waiting at the familiar mark with a newly repaired line glove. Luo watched from beside the replacement without taking over his hand. Han's crane served the private restricted loading interval under its existing business arrangement. The later four-copper public lease was not already earning payment. Yue listened to ordinary cargo sounds return and felt how much she had missed being mildly annoyed by them.

canal_p17_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_062.text: The gardener's daughter stayed after supper to ask Pei about work outside the family plot. She liked keeping counts but did not want to spend every season measuring damaged beans. Pei offered to show her the clerk's actual apprentice tasks at a later agreed hour, with no appointment made through her father's claim. Her father heard from the door and said she would be needed at harvest. She said the clerk's hour came after sorting. Yue watched him consider a child's future that did not have to abandon one place to visit another.

canal_p17_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_063.text: Han slept badly before the remittance and woke his wife by reaching for the counted box. She put her hand on the lid and told him the clerk had not learned arithmetic in the last two hours. He left it shut. At dawn, she served barley tea and asked whether he would keep the repaired shoes on display. He said they were too fragile. She found a small lined drawer instead. The chest had returned damp, but not everything in the family had to live permanently on a table where people discussed loss.

canal_p17_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_064.text: On the forty-first morning, Han brought the counted forty-eight to the authorized private receiver. The clerk checked the amount with both parties and recorded actual refund under the deposit contract. The agent gave the named buyer's receipt and signed release of its specified gear security. Han received his counterpart before the purse left. The main crane, platforms and listed empty chests no longer stood under that deposit charge. The public canal bed remained where it had always been, outside this private transfer.

canal_p17_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_065.text: The store workers watched the completed release from their ordinary receiving space. One asked whether the crane would still need its restricted swing. Its repair limits remained exactly what the current test established. Freedom from private security did not enlarge wood or iron. Han told him the chalk arc and next paid shift stayed posted. The worker nodded and went to check his own hook. Yue saw relief without a sudden transformation into applause. People could keep earning at a wharf that no longer waited to be taken away.

canal_p17_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_066.text: The buyer's agent left with the completed receipt and authority counterpart. Tian gave him his forgotten tea cup from the store doorway because Han's wife wanted it washed, not exported. He laughed and handed it back. On the path, the porter he had once nearly obstructed with a rope loop called him behind the ordinary waiting board. This time he moved there before being asked twice. Yue watched his expensive boots stand in the right small place while a grain boat's loaded line passed.

canal_p17_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_067.text: Han's remaining fifty-six toll claim stayed with its actual original terms, and the lease counterpart stayed with its later service start. Pei amended the public receiving display to show the completed private deposit only in the limited incident account Han had offered. The public debt sheet did not lose fifty-six because somebody saw forty-eight leave another box. Yue read the two records once, then put the cover back. There would be other mornings when confusion returned; today the actual money had gone where its contract said it should.

canal_p17_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_068.text: Bao tried the support strap with the clinician's approved light movement and found the cloth comfortable but his grip still weak. He wanted to help cut the old sale board into Han's wife's shelf. The separate household carpenter had accepted that private job. Bao made a face and said everybody seemed capable of replacing him lately. Luo heard him and sat beside his chair. 'It is rude of them,' she said. 'We must recover enough to be useful elsewhere.' Yue smiled and left them the tilted diagram board.

canal_p17_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_069.text: The gardener received the proper cause-review acknowledgment through his chosen household contact. The owner and reed gatherer had their dates too. The earlier offer of aid stayed fulfilled while those questions moved. The quarry's ordinary outlet correction had passed its accessible receiving check, according to the officer's current public report. The next heavy rain would meet a wider channel, though no report promised a flood could never come again. Yue delivered the current fact and let the gardener decide whether to find it comforting.

canal_p17_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_070.text: At the house, the grandmother planted a sound mint cutting her son brought from his own checked garden stock. It went into the cleaned jar on the repaired window ledge. Yue helped add a little ordinary water after being asked. The old lost herbs had not returned. The plant was new, with a root her son could actually point to. He said the jar looked happier. His mother said jars had excellent manners and never contradicted gardeners. Yue laughed until the owner came to ask what noise had invaded her doorway.

canal_p17_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_071.text: Tian accepted a new sail order whose deadline fell after the canal commission closed. She would remain at her own rented room while Yue left for the orchard appointment if accepted. They discussed supper during the remaining weeks without making each meal a farewell rehearsal. Yue wanted to stay for the sail's first fit. Tian said it might be beautiful and late, which was a poor basis for changing a promised journey. She gave Yue a scrap for sketching and kept the customer's actual cloth on her own bench.

canal_p17_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_072.text: The young keeper arrived for his scheduled practical check at the main gate. Luo asked him to read the fixed reference before touching the handle. He did, then noticed an ordinary loose twig at the accessible guide edge. The feeder isolation and reachable removal followed the posted small procedure. The twig left, and the gate moved. Yue thought of the child's whistle caught on her first day. The familiar tiny problem now had another pair of competent hands, and Luo watched without reaching for the pole herself.

canal_p17_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_073.text: At noon, Han's wife took the canceled sale board to the household carpenter. The accepted private job cut it into a shelf for dry wrapping cloth. Han kept a small corner bearing his former seal in a drawer, with her agreement. Yue helped carry the light offcut away at his request. Tian asked whether the shelf included annual household obligations. Han said only a duty to remain level. Bao laughed from his supported chair and warned that wood seldom read contracts carefully enough for that.

canal_p17_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_074.text: The child whose broken market pot had been uncovered came to admire Han's new shelf. He asked whether his own pretend shop could rent its lower corner. Han said wrapping cloth would fill it before supper. The child offered three pebbles and a button. Han's wife inspected the button gravely and said it might be useful if its owner agreed to part with it. The child reconsidered, tucked it away and went to build his shop beneath the public willow, where his grandmother could see him.

canal_p17_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_075.text: Luo made cabbage stew at the keeper's hearth that evening. Bao tried to steady a bowl with his supported wrist and spilled a little broth before admitting he needed the table closer. Tian moved it without comment. Han arrived carrying the old canceled notice's small cut corner and asked where he should keep it. Luo pointed to the stew shelf and said paper survived better in a drawer. He laughed and put it inside his coat. Yue ate two bowls and discovered she was hungry enough to stop discussing the bank.

canal_p17_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_076.text: The emergency and relief papers entered their assigned archives after the final counterparts reached recipients. The apparatus stayed at the commission store with its exact charge record and no operator silently retained beyond her completed appointment. The original repair account still had closing checks during the remaining weeks. Yue helped place the covered papers on the proper shelf rather than binding every story into one grand volume. Pei asked her to leave space for the next day's ordinary entry. Yue moved the stack a finger's width.

canal_p17_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_077.text: After supper, Luo showed Yue the proposed later operating rota. It had named actual staff and contacts, but the clerk copied a few old household headings at its edge for convenience. Tian frowned at those headings. The operator had two winter mornings; the gardener had no standing public work turn; the reed gatherer wanted notices at his seasonal shelter. Yue could see tomorrow's discussion approaching. They would have to make a useful schedule without letting a familiar page quietly turn neighbors back into available hands.

canal_p17_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p17_078.text: Before sleep, Han sent a short note thanking the clerk for completing the refund within its real period. He did not ask the note to say the sale notice had never caused harm. Yue read his offered public sentence and approved only the completed remittance wording. Then she put away the day's accounts and drew the new shelf beside Tian's plant from memory. On the forty-second morning, names would go onto the later work rota, and the hardest part would be remembering that a name could identify a person without promising the bank her whole future.
